      - term: United Kingdom
      - definition:
        - text: The UK sorts products the same way, by claim, form and use, into cosmetics, food and medicines; lesson 7.2 set out its route for unlicensed medicines.
        - generic: "Source: A guide to what is a medicinal product — MHRA Guidance Note 8"
      - term: European Union
      - definition:
        - text: In the EU, a product is a medicine by presentation or by pharmacological, immunological or metabolic function, and where it could also fall under another product law, medicines law applies (Directive 2001/83/EC, Articles 1(2) and 2(2)); anything intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted is not a cosmetic (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Article 2(2)). Food supplements are foods, and a health claim on a food is prohibited unless it is authorised and on the EU lists of authorised claims (Directive 2002/46/EC; Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006, Article 10(1)).
        - generic: "Source: Directive 2001/83/EC on the Community code relating to medicinal products for human use (consolidated text of 1 January 2025) · Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products (consolidated text of 18 May 2026) · Directive 2002/46/EC on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to food supplements (consolidated text of 26 November 2025) · Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 on nutrition and health claims made on foods (consolidated text of 13 December 2014)"
      - term: Portugal
      - definition:
        - text: In Portugal, INFARMED is the competent authority for cosmetics and states that products administered by ingestion, inhalation, injection or implantation into the body are not cosmetics (read 25 September 2026). Food supplements are meant to maintain the body's homeostasis, not to prevent, treat or cure disease, and must be notified to DGAV before sale; DGAV warns that notification does not mean a supplement is authorised or compliant.
        - generic: "Source: Decreto-Lei n.º 23/2025, de 19 de março – assegura a execução, na ordem jurídica interna, do Regulamento (CE) n.º 1223/2009 (produtos cosméticos) · Perguntas frequentes – Cosméticos · Suplementos Alimentares · Procedimento de Notificação de Suplementos Alimentares"
      - term: Brazil
      - definition:
        - text: In Brazil, cosmetic labelling may not carry therapeutic claims for the product or its ingredients (RDC 907/2024, art. 12), and ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that injectable cosmetics do not exist and that, if a product is offered in this form, it is an irregular cosmetic. A food supplement is by definition a product for oral ingestion by healthy people (RDC 243/2018), and it may use only constituents on ANVISA's authorised list (IN 28/2018).
        - generic: "Source: Resolução RDC nº 907, de 19 de setembro de 2024 (produtos de higiene pessoal, cosméticos e perfumes) · Checamos: peptídeos que prometem milagres NÃO estão registrados na Anvisa · Consulta de cosméticos regularizados (TA_CONSULTA_COSMETICOS.CSV) · Resolução-RE nº 1.771, de 29 de abril de 2026 · Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada – RDC nº 243, de 26 de julho de 2018 (suplementos alimentares) · Ingredientes autorizados – suplementos alimentares"
      - term: United Arab Emirates
      - definition:
        - text: In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 makes cosmetics with a medical effect on the skin, hair or nails, and food supplements, medical products regulated by the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE, the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023), while ordinary cosmetics need a MoIAT conformity certificate (Cabinet Resolution 18/2014); an EDE classification letter settles whether a product needs EDE marketing authorisation and in which regulatory category. In Abu Dhabi, the DoH keeps topical cosmetic peptides with no systemic effect on existing pathways as low-risk products, while systemic, regenerative or weakly evidenced peptides face enhanced controls (31 July 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Federal Decree-Law No. (28) of 2023 On the Establishment of the UAE Drug Corporation (official English translation) · Federal Decree-Law No. (38) of 2024 Governing Medical Products, Pharmacists and Pharmaceutical Establishments (official English translation) · قائمة بمتطلبات جميع التشريعات و الأنظمة الرقابية الخاصة بالمنتجات (List of technical requirements for regulated products, 'CAD Regulated Sheet') · Issue Conformity Certificates for Regulated Products (ECAS) (service page) · Classification of a Medical Product (service page) · DoH Circular No. (148)/2026: Mandatory Requirements for Peptide Products"
      - term: Saudi Arabia
      - definition: "Saudi context: check each cosmetic or collagen supplement’s category, record and claims separately. Listing a topical product does not establish permission to inject the same ingredient; registering a supplement does not establish efficacy for treating skin disease. Exact commercial-product verification remains incomplete."
    - paragraph: Route and claim decide the regime, whatever the molecule. Here is how each one treats a skin peptide in the US, as checked in September 2026.
    - strong: Cosmetic
    - generic: Appearance claims only
    - generic: No premarket approval. A claim to affect structure or function, such as 'regenerates cells', makes it a drug; 'cosmeceutical' has no legal meaning.
    - strong: Dietary supplement
    - generic: Oral, no disease claims
    - generic: The maker is responsible for safety and labelling before sale; FDA acts after products reach the market.
    - strong: Approved drug
    - generic: Labelled indications
    - generic: Off-label use of an approved drug is lawful clinical judgment; document the reasoning.
    - strong: Compounded (503A or 503B)
    - generic: Unapproved, conditionally lawful
    - generic: Only when the substance qualifies and the pharmacy meets the statute. Non-injectable GHK-Cu is in Category 1; BPC-157 and TB-500 have no route.
    - strong: Investigational or research use only
    - generic: Trials, or nothing
    - generic: Human use belongs in a clinical trial. A 'research use only' vial is outside any clinical route.
    - paragraph: Write the regime in the chart in these words, before anything else.
